root_cause.text: The `fib6_is_reject()` function incorrectly classifies standalone IPv6 nexthop objects with a loopback device as reject routes because nexthop objects have no destination prefix (fc_dst=::), causing `fib6_nh_init()` to skip `fib_nh_common_init()` and leave `nhc_pcpu_rth_output` unallocated; later dereference of this NULL pointer by an IPv4 route referencing the nexthop results in a panic.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "nexthop objects have no destination prefix (fc_dst=::), causing fib6_is_reject() to match any loopback nexthop. The reject path skips fib_nh_common_init(), leaving nhc_pcpu_rth_output unallocated. If an IPv4 route later references this nexthop, __mkroute_output() dereferences NULL nhc_pcpu_rth_output and panics." The patch changes the condition from `fib6_is_reject(cfg->fc_flags, dev, addr_type)` to `cfg->fc_flags & RTF_REJECT`, directly fixing the misclassification.

Further nested inside the reject branch; if dev is NULL (which can happen for nexthop objects without a device), this condition fails, leading to incomplete initialization and eventual NULL pointer dereference when the nexthop is used by an IPv4 route.
